evidence: Starting from Upper Caples Valley junction (sign-posted), the track goes uphill through the beech forest.
The track then continues from the saddle down to Steele Creek and follows the creek.
Once at Steele Creek Hut, the track descends into the forest, windfall might be present until you reach the Greenstone valley.

doubts: One way: the track is described from the Upper Caples junction down to the Greenstone valley, so it is recorded as one way. The start and end are given as junctions and a valley with no feature or name entry, so their refs are null. The Greenstone Road end/car park and the Divide car park are the other routes that reach the junctions; they are recorded as access points, and the Greenstone leg from the junction to the road end is recorded as an exit. The page gives no time for the Steele Creek Track itself (the times in Getting there are for the connecting walks), so time is null; the distance of 15 km one way is DOC's summary. The saddle the track climbs to is taken as the Steele Creek pass (1359 m) that the page mentions in winter; it is not matched to McKellar Saddle. The creek crossings are described only as 'multiple creeks, normally low when dry', so none is recorded. Pass Burn and Slip Flat are in the names list but are not walked on this track, so they are left out.
